job.title: Procurement Officer
job.description:
Melbourne | Full Time, Permanent | $80,000 - $85,000 Package (Inclusive of Super)

The Organisation

Our client operates within Melbourne's major events and entertainment sector, delivering world-class experiences enjoyed by millions of visitors each year.

With a strong focus on collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement, they are seeking a Procurement Officer to join their growing procurement function. You'll become part of a close-knit team that values development, knowledge-sharing and supporting one another to achieve outcomes.

This team has a strong track record of developing people, making it an ideal environment for someone looking to establish a genuine career in procurement.

The Role

This Procurement Officer position sits within a growing procurement function and is suited to someone with 2-3 years' procurement, purchasing or contract administration experience looking to take the next step in their career.

Working alongside experienced Procurement Specialists, you'll support sourcing activities, supplier onboarding, contract management and procurement operations across a diverse stakeholder group. The role offers broad exposure across the procurement lifecycle while providing ongoing development and mentorship from an experienced team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support day-to-day procurement and purchasing activities
  • Assist with supplier onboarding and contract administration
  • Support sourcing activities, quotations and tender processes
  • Maintain procurement records, reporting and contract documentation
  • Work across contract management and procurement systems
  • Respond to stakeholder enquiries and provide procurement support
  • Assist with contract renewals and procurement compliance activities
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives across the procurement function

About You

We're looking for someone with the aptitude and desire to build a long-term career in procurement.

You'll bring:

  • A degree, graduate diploma, MBA or postgraduate qualification in Business, Commerce, Procurement, Supply Chain, Law or a related discipline
  • 2-3 years' experience within procurement, purchasing, sourcing or contract administration
  • Exposure to supplier onboarding, purchasing processes and contract administration
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational capability
  • Confidence working across procurement and ERP systems
  • A proactive, customer-focused approach to supporting the business
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • The ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment


What's On Offer

This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career procurement professional to accelerate their development within a well-established procurement function.

You'll gain exposure to sourcing, contract management and supplier engagement activities while partnering with stakeholders across a high-profile organisation. Supported by experienced procurement leaders, you'll have the opportunity to broaden your capability and continue building a long-term career in procurement.

Interested?

If you're looking for a role that offers genuine development, strong mentoring and a clear pathway into procurement, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Compliance Manager
job.description:
About Plenary
Quinn Allan is proud to partner with Plenary, a leading global infrastructure investor, developer and funds management business operating across Australia, New Zealand, Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

As the organisation continues to grow in scale and complexity, Plenary is seeking a commercially minded Compliance Manager to support the ongoing evolution of its Governance & Compliance function and help strengthen governance, regulatory and compliance capability across the business.

About the Position
Reporting to the Director - Governance & Compliance, this newly created role offers the opportunity to play a key role in supporting Plenary's compliance obligations across multiple jurisdictions.

Working within a lean and highly collaborative team, you will support compliance, AML/CTF, governance, regulatory change and risk management activities while helping mature frameworks, improve processes and strengthen the overall compliance function.

This is not a maintenance-style compliance role. Instead, it offers the opportunity to build, influence and improve, making it ideal for someone who enjoys creating structure, navigating ambiguity and partnering closely with stakeholders to deliver practical outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and monitor compliance obligations across multiple regulatory frameworks
  • Support AML/CTF compliance activities, monitoring and reporting requirements
  • Maintain compliance registers, policies, controls and governance documentation
  • Monitor regulatory developments and support implementation of regulatory change
  • Support compliance reporting, monitoring activities and governance forums
  • Assist with internal audits, external audits and regulatory reviews
  • Support third-party risk management and due diligence activities
  • Contribute to process improvement, automation and compliance uplift initiatives
  • Build strong relationships with stakeholders across the business

About You
You may currently be working as a Compliance Manager, Senior Compliance Officer, Compliance Advisor, AML/CTF Specialist or Governance & Compliance professional within a regulated environment.

You will bring:

  • Experience within financial services, funds management, infrastructure investment or a similarly regulated industry
  • Strong understanding of compliance frameworks and regulatory obligations
  • Strong experience with AML/CTF requirements and governance processes
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • Commercial judgement and a pragmatic approach to compliance
  • The ability to work autonomously and thrive in an evolving environment

Exposure to AFSL obligations, multi-jurisdiction compliance frameworks and governance platforms such as Diligent One will be highly regarded.

Why Join Plenary?

  • Leading global infrastructure investment business
  • Newly created position with genuine scope and impact
  • Opportunity to help shape and mature the compliance function
  • Significant autonomy and stakeholder exposure
  • Collaborative, low-ego and professional culture
  • Exposure to complex international regulatory environments

This is an excellent opportunity for a compliance professional looking to step into a broad and influential role within a highly regarded global organisation.

How to Apply

job.title: Senior Commercial Analyst
job.description:
Quinn Allan is partnering with a well-established and growing organisation based in Clayton operating within a specialist industrial and technology-driven environment.

The business has built a strong reputation within its sector through a customer-centric approach, long-term client relationships and an ongoing commitment to innovation. Backed by a recognised global brand, the organisation combines the stability and resources of a multinational business with the agility and accessibility of a smaller local operation.
With a collaborative and commercially focused culture, employees enjoy direct access to senior leadership, broad responsibilities and the opportunity to make a genuine impact on business performance. The organisation continues to invest in future growth opportunities, creating an exciting environment for ambitious professionals looking to develop their careers.


About the Position
Reporting directly to the Finance Director, this newly positioned Senior Commercial Analyst role will play a key role in supporting commercial decision-making across the business.
Working closely with Sales, Service, Marketing and Operations, you will provide insight and analysis that helps drive pricing decisions, customer profitability, commercial performance and future growth initiatives.
A significant focus of the role will be supporting customer opportunities, evaluating pricing structures, analysing margins and helping stakeholders understand the long-term commercial impact of key business decisions. Given the nature of the business, every deal is different, creating a highly interesting and commercially focused environment.
Alongside the business partnering responsibilities, you will take ownership of budgeting, forecasting, management reporting and performance analysis, providing valuable insights to senior leadership and helping shape future business strategy.
This opportunity has arisen following an internal promotion and represents an excellent opportunity for an ambitious finance professional seeking broader exposure and long-term career progression.


Duties
• Partner with Sales, Service and Operational leaders to support commercial decision-making
• Analyse pricing, margins and customer profitability across the business
• Support evaluation of major customer opportunities and commercial proposals
• Develop financial insights and recommendations to support growth and profitability
• Lead budgeting and forecasting processes across multiple business areas
• Prepare monthly management reports and performance analysis
• Conduct variance analysis and provide commentary on business performance
• Support annual business planning and strategic initiatives
• Work closely with stakeholders to assess commercial opportunities and risks
• Assist with customer investment appraisals and financial evaluations
• Identify trends, opportunities and drivers of business performance
• Support development of financial models and decision-support tools
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across finance and operations
• Provide guidance and support to internal finance stakeholders
• Build strong working relationships across finance, sales and leadership teams


About You
You will be a commercially minded finance professional who enjoys partnering with stakeholders, solving problems and influencing business outcomes.
You may currently be working as a Senior Commercial Analyst, Senior Management Accountant, Finance Business Partner or Financial Analyst and be looking for an opportunity to broaden your commercial exposure within a growing and highly visible business.
Experience within manufacturing, industrial products, capital equipment, distribution, logistics or other product-based environments will be highly regarded, although candidates from other industries with strong commercial finance experience are encouraged to apply.

You will have:
• CA or CPA qualification
• Experience in budgeting, forecasting and management reporting
• Strong commercial analysis and business partnering capability
• Exposure to pricing, margin analysis or customer profitability reporting
• Experience supporting sales, operational or commercial stakeholders
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Advanced Excel capability and confidence working with financial data
• Ability to communicate financial information to non-finance stakeholders
• Strong attention to detail and commercial judgement
• A proactive and solutions-focused approach
• The desire to learn, develop and take on increasing responsibility

Most importantly, we are seeking someone who is ambitious, commercially curious and eager to accelerate their career. This role will suit someone looking to move beyond traditional reporting and gain exposure to commercial decision-making, executive stakeholders and broader business strategy.


How to Apply
Please click 'Apply' to submit your resume online, or contact Olivia Reiber on oreiber@quinnallan.com.au for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Finance Planning & Analysis Lead
job.description:
About the Company

Medical Indemnity Protection Society (MIPS) is a member-focused organisation providing protection, advice and support to healthcare professionals across Australia.

The organisation is entering an important period of transformation, with continued investment in systems, data and broader business capability. Finance is central to this journey, with an increasing focus on stronger business partnering, better management information and sharper commercial insight. This is an exciting opportunity to join an evolving finance function and help shape how MIPS measures performance and supports decision-making across the organisation.



About the Role

Reporting to the Financial Controller, the Financial Planning and Analysis Lead (FP&A Lead) will take ownership of budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, KPI reporting and performance analysis, while partnering closely with executives and senior leaders across the business.

The role will focus on understanding the drivers of performance, providing meaningful commercial insight and helping stakeholders make better-informed decisions. You will work closely with leaders across MIPS to constructively challenge thinking, strengthen financial understanding and further establish finance as a valued business partner.

A key part of the opportunity is to modernise planning and reporting processes, reduce manual activity and explore how automation, AI and emerging technology can improve the quality, timeliness and efficiency of financial information.



You will be responsible for:

  • Lead the budgeting and forecasting process across the organisation
  • Deliver meaningful management reporting, KPI analysis and performance insights
  • Partner with executives and senior stakeholders to support commercial and strategic decision-making
  • Translate complex financial information into clear, practical insights for non-finance stakeholders
  • Identify trends, risks and opportunities across financial and non-financial performance
  • Improve financial planning, reporting and analysis processes
  • Support the organisation's broader transformation agenda
  • Identify opportunities to use automation, AI and technology to streamline finance processes and reporting
  • Lead, coach and develop two direct reports.


About You

You are a commercially minded finance professional who enjoys partnering with the business and using financial information to influence better decisions. Naturally curious and confident engaging with senior leaders, you are comfortable asking questions, constructively challenging thinking and translating complex financial information into clear, practical insights.



You will bring:

  • Strong FP&A experience across budgeting, forecasting, management reporting and financial analysis
  • Proven ability to partner with and influence senior stakeholders
  • Experience within insurance, financial services or another regulated environment
  • Strong analytical capability and the ability to turn financial data into meaningful business insights
  • A track record of improving reporting, financial processes and ways of working
  • Leadership, coaching or mentoring experience, with an interest in developing team capability
  • A degree in Accounting, Commerce or Business
  • CPA, CA or similar qualification.

This role offers genuine career progression for someone with the capability and ambition to develop into broader finance leadership responsibilities over time.


Next Steps
Please submit your application today by clicking 'Apply' or contact Rachel Morton on 0429 070 743 for further information.

job.description:
If Risk and Quality are your areas of specialisation within health or community and a new role is in your sights, review this!

The Organisation
This organisation plays a critical role in strengthening primary care, improving access to services and driving integration across the health system. With a particular focus on equity, population health outcomes and innovation, their aim is to deliver impact with measurable goals that produce better health outcomes for communities.

The Role
This is a newly created leadership role that will steward best practice for Risk and Quality across the organisation.
Working closely with senior stakeholders across the organisation, your remit is to lead their key pillars, strengthen organisational controls and frameworks ensuring all leaders receive credible information for informed decisions.

This role will lead continuous improvement for risk management, governance and reporting, quality management, internal audits and assurance and policy governance. There will be a review of insurances where you will be the liaison with external negotiations, you will support all audit cycles with external providers including all planning, coordination and progress reporting. This position will oversee incident and feedback reporting processes including complaints and improvement suggestions and also lead the development, review and implementation of the organisational policies and procedures.
Responsibility will also include leading implementation and continuous improvement for ISO9001.
This is a highly visible role with many touchpoints throughout the organisation. As such it is critical that the successful candidate models the desired culture and demonstrates leadership through role modelling and delivery of work practices.

The Fit
The ideal candidate will possess the necessary qualifications that reflect best practice in risk and quality. Post graduate quals are preferred. Combining quals with significant experience, ideally gained in a similar sector where there is an appreciation of the nuances of health and not for profit would be preferred, demonstrated experience working with senior stakeholders is non-negotiable. Experience working with a ticketing system, ISO27001 ISMS and exposure to Ai is ideal, systems literate, solutions focused, able to negotiate and influence with high level communications is expected. Salary commensurate with experience, circa $155k plus super and SP.

What's Next
